rows.name: Barbell Standing Ab Rollout
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you roll out, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Brace the abs and tuck the pelvis before rolling
Roll out only as far as your lower back stays flat
Pull back with the abs, not the hips
common_mistakes: Sagging lower back at full stretch
Hips piking up on the way back
rows.pro_tip: Start from the knees or use a wall stop before going standing
rows.indian_alternative: Ab wheel or towel slide on a smooth floor
rows.note: Standing barbell rollout is very advanced; barbell loaded with plates acts as the wheel. Check picture for knees vs standing.

rows.name: Suspended Abdominal Fallout

rows.indian_alternative: Towel slide fallout on a smooth floor

rows.name: Dumbbell Standing Front Raise Above Head

coaching_cues: Raise both dumbbells forward and up until the arms are overhead

Lower slowly, no swing
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to lift
Using weights too heavy for the overhead range

rows.indian_alternative: Raise a pair of water bottles overhead

Heels lifting or knees caving in

rows.name: Isometric Chest Squeeze

Squeeze as hard as you can while keeping the shoulders down
Keep elbows level with the hands

Shrugging the shoulders up
rows.pro_tip: Squeeze at about 70% effort for the full hold
rows.note: Assumed palm-press isometric; check picture.

rows.name: Medicine Ball Supine Chest Throw
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as you throw

Throw straight up as fast as you can
Catch softly with bent elbows and repeat
common_mistakes: Throwing off-line so the ball drifts away
Catching with locked elbows

rows.name: Assisted Chin Up

Lower fully with control
common_mistakes: Using too much assistance for too long
Shrugging and cutting the range short
rows.pro_tip: Reduce the assistance weight a little each week

rows.name: Standing Assisted Chin Up

coaching_cues: Stand on the assist platform and grip the handles, palms toward you

Lower slowly, fully extending the arms

Half reps

rows.name: Close Grip Chin Up

Lower to a full hang
common_mistakes: Kipping or swinging

rows.name: Narrow Neutral Grip Chin Up

coaching_cues: Hinge forward under the bar with a wide overhand grip
Row the bar toward the chest with elbows flared out
Squeeze the rear delts, lower slowly
common_mistakes: Shrugging the traps and rowing with the lats
Using momentum from the hips
rows.pro_tip: Go light; rear delts respond to the squeeze, not the load

rows.name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe slowly and relax deeper on each exhale
coaching_cues: Bring one arm across the chest at shoulder height
Pull it in gently with the other hand or forearm
Keep the shoulder down, do not rotate the torso
common_mistakes: Bouncing in the stretch
Holding the breath or forcing the range
rows.pro_tip: Hold 30-60 seconds; repeat on the other side

rows.name: Decline Depth Pushup
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you drop, exhale as you explode up
coaching_cues: Start with hands on raised platforms, body rigid
Drop the hands to the floor, absorbing with the chest
Explode up immediately and repeat
common_mistakes: Sagging hips on landing
Pausing at the bottom, losing the rebound
rows.pro_tip: Master clapping and plyo push-ups before adding the drop
rows.note: Name says Decline, folder says Incline Push Up Depth Jump. Check picture: feet raised vs hands raised.

rows.name: Seated Dip
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Sit on the bench edge, hands beside the hips
Slide off and lower the hips until the elbows reach about 90 degrees
Press up to straight arms, keeping the hips close
common_mistakes: Sinking too deep and straining the shoulders
Flaring the elbows out
rows.pro_tip: Bend the knees to make it easier, straighten them to progress
rows.note: Assumed bench dip (seated start); check picture.

rows.name: Single Arm Dip
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Support yourself on one arm, other arm held out
Keep the body tight and slightly turned, lower slowly
Press up to full extension without twisting
common_mistakes: Dropping fast without control
Using the free hand for balance
rows.pro_tip: Work through weighted dips and archer dips first
rows.note: Draft 'bodyweight'; one-arm dip is normally on bars, but picture may show a bench or other support. Check picture.

hold.reason: low-confidence draft with no picture read; the drafted identity is unchecked

rows.name: Weighted Close Grip Chin Up on Dip Cage
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hang from the bar with a close underhand grip, weight on the belt
Pull the chest toward the bar, elbows close
Lower to a full hang with control
common_mistakes: Kipping or swinging with the added weight
Cutting the range short
rows.pro_tip: Add weight only after 3x8 clean bodyweight chin-ups
rows.note: Draft 'other'. Assumed dip belt or weight plate; the 'dip cage' is the bar station.

hold.reason: raw equipment token dip belt maps to nothing in EquipmentVocab; Batch D owns the tokens

rows.name: Tricep Dips Floor
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Sit on the floor, hands behind the hips with fingers forward
Lift the hips and bend the elbows to lower
Press up to straight arms
common_mistakes: Hands placed too far behind, straining the shoulders
Shrugging the shoulders up
rows.pro_tip: Keep the hips close to the hands to protect the shoulders
rows.note: Assumed floor (reverse) dip; check picture.

rows.name: Kettlebell Double Snatch
rows.breathing_cue: Brace before the pull, exhale as the bells lock out
coaching_cues: Swing both bells back between the legs with a flat back
Snap the hips and pull the elbows high, punching through overhead
Lock out over the shoulders and lower under control
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of the hips
Slamming the bells onto the forearms
rows.pro_tip: Master the single-arm snatch first
rows.note: Two kettlebells (double) per name; check picture.

rows.name: Kettlebell Double Windmill
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you return to standing
coaching_cues: Lock out one bell overhead and keep your eyes on it
Push the hip out and hinge, lowering the other hand toward the foot
Return to standing, keeping the arm locked
common_mistakes: Bending the overhead arm
Rounding the back instead of hinging
rows.pro_tip: Learn the windmill unloaded, then with a light bell
rows.note: Double windmill: bells in both hands; check picture.

rows.name: Cable Up Down Twist
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Stand sideways to the cable, handle held with both hands
Rotate the torso and sweep the handle across the body, up or down
Keep the hips square and control the return
common_mistakes: Using the arms instead of the torso
Over-rotating through the lower back
rows.pro_tip: Pivot the back foot so the lower back is not twisted
rows.note: Chop/lift-type cable rotation; check picture for direction.

rows.name: Barbell Drag Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Keep the bar in contact with the body and drag it up
Pull the elbows back as the bar rises
Squeeze, then lower along the same path
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso
Letting the bar drift away from the body
rows.pro_tip: Drag curls reduce front-delt help and bias the long head

rows.name: Cable Drag Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Pull the elbows back as the handle rises along the body
Squeeze at the top
Lower along the same path
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso
Letting the cable drift away from the body
rows.pro_tip: Drag curls reduce front-delt help and bias the long head

rows.name: Elbow Dips
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press up
coaching_cues: Hold parallel bars, torso fairly upright
Keep elbows tight to the ribs on the way down
Press up until elbows fully lock out
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows wide
Dropping too deep and overloading the shoulders
rows.pro_tip: Do bench dips first if you cannot do 8 clean reps
rows.indian_alternative: Two sturdy chairs placed side by side
rows.note: Assumed a triceps-biased bar dip with elbows tucked; check the picture (could be a bench/elbow-support variant).

rows.name: Dumbbell Lying Elbow Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, dumbbells over chest
Keep upper arms still, only forearms move
Press up until arms are straight
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows
Letting the weights drift toward the face fast
rows.pro_tip: Start light: this hits the long head and stresses elbows
rows.indian_alternative: Two water bottles or filled bags
rows.note: Assumed a lying dumbbell triceps extension/press with elbows pointing up; equipment draft has no bench so floor or bench both work.

rows.name: Elliptical Trainer
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe rhythmically with the stride
coaching_cues: Stand tall, hands on the moving handles
Push through the whole foot each stride
Keep a steady rhythm, no hanging on the rails
common_mistakes: Leaning on the console
Bouncing with tiny choppy strides
rows.pro_tip: Alternate 1 min hard with 2 min easy for intervals
rows.note: Renamed from "Elliptical (Time)".

rows.name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, exhale as you fold forward
coaching_cues: Sit tall on the edge of a chair, one leg extended straight out in front
Hinge from the hips with a flat back
Hold, then switch legs
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to reach the toes
Forcing the knee into hyperextension
rows.pro_tip: Pull toes toward you to add a gentle calf stretch
rows.note: Chair is mapped to elevated surface (no chair token). Check picture: seated vs standing foot on chair.

rows.name: Resistance Band Leg Extension
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the knee
coaching_cues: Sit on a bench, band looped around ankle and anchored
Straighten the knee fully and squeeze the quad
Return slowly to the start
common_mistakes: Swinging the leg with momentum
Leaning back to cheat the last reps
rows.pro_tip: Pause 1 second at the top for a harder squeeze
rows.indian_alternative: Dupatta or tied cloth strip anchored low is a weak substitute
rows.note: Assumed seated band leg extension; check if single-leg or double-leg and whether a foot anchor is needed.

rows.name: Dumbbell Cross Face Lying Extension
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the elbow
coaching_cues: Lie back, dumbbell held over the shoulder
Lower it across the face toward the opposite shoulder
Extend the elbow back up to lockout
common_mistakes: Letting the upper arm drift out of position
Using a weight too heavy to control near the face
rows.pro_tip: Keep the upper arm still; only the elbow bends
rows.note: Assumed single-arm cross-body lying triceps extension; check picture.

rows.name: EZ Bar Decline Close Grip Face Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as the bar lowers, exhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, EZ bar over chest
Bend only at the elbows to lower toward the forehead
Press back up without flaring the elbows
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift wide
Bouncing the bar off the forehead
rows.pro_tip: Use a spotter or light weight, the bar travels near your face
rows.note: Assumed decline close-grip skull crusher; a decline bench may not be available, flat bench works.

rows.name: Upward Facing Dog
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lift the chest, exhale to settle
coaching_cues: Lie face down, hands beside the ribs
Press up, straighten arms, lift thighs off the floor
Open the chest, shoulders away from the ears
common_mistakes: Crunching the neck back
Dumping weight into the lower back
rows.pro_tip: Keep glutes lightly engaged to protect the lower back

rows.name: Farmers Walk
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe steadily and stay braced
coaching_cues: Stand tall with a heavy dumbbell in each hand
Keep shoulders back and ribs down
Take short, quick steps in a straight line
common_mistakes: Swaying side to side
Letting the shoulders shrug up
rows.pro_tip: Grip as hard as you can; it builds the forearms too
rows.note: Duplicate of library E089 Farmers Carry (same movement); consider merging.

rows.name: Kettlebell Figure 8
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe steadily through each pass
coaching_cues: Stand wide, hinge with a flat back
Pass the kettlebell between and around the legs in a figure 8
Keep your chest up and hips low
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Dropping the bell when handing it off
rows.pro_tip: Start with a light bell until the hand-offs feel smooth

rows.name: Dumbbell Finger Curls
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the fingers curl in
coaching_cues: Sit with forearms resting on thighs, palms up
Let the dumbbell roll to the fingertips
Curl the fingers closed, then the wrist
common_mistakes: Using heavy weight and losing the dumbbell
Lifting the forearms off the thighs
rows.pro_tip: Pair with wrist curls for complete forearm work
rows.indian_alternative: Heavy filled bucket handle or water can

rows.name: Barbell Finger Curls
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe normally throughout
coaching_cues: Sit with the forearms resting on the thighs, palms up
Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then curl the fingers closed
Squeeze hard at the closed position
common_mistakes: Doing it too fast
Letting the wrist bend and help
rows.pro_tip: Start light because a heavy bar rolls out of the hands.
rows.note: Equipment draft is bodyweight; likely a finger flexion drill or the dumbbell version without weights. Check the picture.

rows.name: Flag
rows.breathing_cue: Hold a shallow breath, exhale when you come down
coaching_cues: Grip a vertical pole, one hand high, one low
Press the bottom arm and pull with the top arm
Lift the body horizontal, legs together
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips
Skipping lead-ups and straining the shoulders
rows.pro_tip: Train tucked and straddle versions before the full flag
rows.note: Human flag; needs a vertical pole or rail (no token), so equipment left as bodyweight and gym=specialty. Check the picture.

rows.name: Leg Pull in Flat Bench
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the knees come in
coaching_cues: Lie on a flat bench, hands holding the sides
Pull the knees in toward your chest
Lower slowly without touching the floor
common_mistakes: Swinging with momentum
Letting the lower back arch
rows.pro_tip: Curl the pelvis up at the top for more abs
rows.note: Assumed lying knee tuck on a bench; check picture for straight-leg or bent-leg.

rows.name: Lying Leg Raise Flat Bench
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the legs rise
coaching_cues: Lie on a flat bench, hold the edge behind you
Raise straight legs to about 90 degrees
Lower slowly, stop before the heels touch down
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the bench
Swinging the legs for momentum
rows.pro_tip: Bend the knees slightly if the lower back complains

rows.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Floor Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on the floor, bell held in the fist at the shoulder
Lower until the upper arm touches the floor
Press straight up, keeping the wrist stacked
common_mistakes: Letting the bell tip back and bend the wrist
Bouncing the elbow off the floor
rows.pro_tip: Floor stops the elbow: a shoulder-friendly press

rows.name: Cable Floor Seated Wide Grip Row
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you row, inhale on the return
coaching_cues: Sit on the floor, feet braced, chest tall
Pull the wide bar to the upper stomach, elbows flared
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slowly
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso back to heave the weight
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
rows.pro_tip: Wide grip shifts work to rear delts and mid back

rows.name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Slow breaths, relax into the stretch on every exhale
coaching_cues: Lie on your side, legs stacked
Reach the top arm overhead and lengthen the side body
Hold without twisting the hips
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips forward or back
Holding the breath
rows.pro_tip: Reach farther by bending slightly the other way
rows.note: Name is vague; assumed a lateral trunk/lat stretch lying on the floor. Check the picture.

rows.name: Band Reverse Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms open, inhale on the return
coaching_cues: Hold the band at chest height, arms straight
Pull the hands apart, leading with the elbows
Squeeze the shoulder blades for a second
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders
Bending the elbows into a row
rows.pro_tip: Use a lighter band and slow the return

rows.name: Cable Incline Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the hands come together
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench between low cables
Open the arms wide with a slight elbow bend
Bring the hands together over the upper chest
common_mistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows
Dropping the arms too far behind the shoulders
rows.pro_tip: Set the bench at 30 degrees to target the upper chest

rows.name: Dumbbell Decline Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as the arms open, exhale as they close
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, dumbbells over the chest
Lower in a wide arc with soft elbows
Squeeze the weights back together
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and bending the elbows
Dropping the arms below shoulder level
rows.pro_tip: Hook your feet firmly so you stay on the bench

rows.name: Dumbbell Decline Single Arm Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as it closes
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench with one dumbbell
Open the working arm in a wide arc, soft elbow
Bring it back to the midline and squeeze
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to cheat the rep
Letting the elbow bend into a press
rows.pro_tip: Brace the core so the torso does not rotate

rows.name: Dumbbell Incline Single Arm Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as the arm opens, exhale as it closes
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench with one dumbbell
Open the working arm in a wide arc, soft elbow
Bring it back over the upper chest
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to lift
Straightening the elbow into a press
rows.pro_tip: Keep the free arm out of the way or across the chest

rows.name: Machine Seated Reverse Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you open the arms
coaching_cues: Sit facing the pad, chest against it
Pull the handles back in a wide arc, elbows soft
Squeeze the rear delts, return slowly
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders
Letting the weight stack crash between reps
rows.pro_tip: Lighter weight and higher reps work best for rear delts

rows.name: Supported Dumbbell Single Arm Reverse Fly
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the arm lifts
coaching_cues: Rest one hand or chest on a support, hinge forward
Raise the dumbbell out to the side, elbow soft
Lower under control, no swinging
common_mistakes: Using the lower back to heave the weight
Rotating the torso up
rows.pro_tip: Support removes lower-back fatigue so rear delts work
rows.note: Support is probably an incline bench or a hand on a rack; draft lists dumbbells only. Check the picture.

rows.name: Back and Forth Step
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe rhythmically with your steps
coaching_cues: Stand tall, light on the balls of the feet
Step one foot back and forward in a steady rhythm
Swing the arms naturally
common_mistakes: Stomping heavily
Leaning the torso forward
rows.pro_tip: Use as a gentle warm-up before lower-body sets
rows.note: Name is vague; assumed a low-impact stepping warm-up drill. Check the picture.

hold.reason: Picture shows a wide side step with a hand reaching to the floor, but the row is a back-and-forth step with cues to match; founder decides rename, rewrite or drop at the GIF review.

rows.name: Forward Jump
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale on take-off, inhale on a soft landing
coaching_cues: Squat and swing the arms back
Drive the arms forward and jump as far as you can
Land soft on bent knees and hold
common_mistakes: Landing with straight, stiff knees
Letting the knees cave inward on landing
rows.pro_tip: Walk back to the start so each jump is fresh
rows.note: Assumed a standing broad jump; check the picture.

rows.name: Dumbbell Contralateral Forward Lunge
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the step, exhale as you drive up
coaching_cues: Hold a dumbbell on the side opposite the front leg
Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees
Drive through the front heel to stand
common_mistakes: Letting the torso twist toward the weight
Front knee collapsing inward
rows.pro_tip: The opposite-side load makes the core and glute medius work
rows.note: Contralateral = load held opposite the lead leg, assumed from the name.

rows.name: Forward Lunge
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lunge, exhale as you push back
coaching_cues: Step forward and drop the back knee toward the floor
Keep the front shin vertical and torso tall
Push off the front foot to return
common_mistakes: Front knee drifting past the toes and caving in
Short step with the heel lifting
rows.pro_tip: Alternate legs or finish all reps on one side
rows.indian_alternative: Use a dupatta on the floor as a step-length marker

rows.name: Frankenstein Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold the barbell on straight arms out in front, like a zombie
Sit the hips back and down, chest tall
Drive up through the whole foot
common_mistakes: Arms dropping and chest collapsing
Heels lifting off the floor
rows.pro_tip: Extended arms act as a counterweight for depth
rows.note: Assumed bodyweight squat with arms forward (Frankenstein arms); draft says bodyweight.

rows.name: Frog Planche
rows.breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, do not hold
coaching_cues: Squat down, hands on the floor with fingers turned out
Rest knees on the elbows and lean forward
Lift the feet off the floor and hold
common_mistakes: Not leaning forward enough
Letting the shoulders sink between the hands
rows.pro_tip: Warm up the wrists thoroughly before holds
rows.note: Planche lead-up (frog stand / tuck). Next step name not known in this chunk; progression_to left null.

rows.name: Barbell Rollout From Bench
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the bar back in
coaching_cues: Kneel at the end of a bench, hands on a loaded bar
Roll the bar forward with a tight, hollow body
Pull back using the abs, not the hips
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back sag
Rolling out farther than you can control
rows.pro_tip: Start with short rollouts and add range weekly
rows.note: Assumed kneeling on a bench rolling a barbell; ab wheel version is a separate family member. Check the picture.

rows.name: Weighted Front Plank
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe steadily, do not hold your breath
coaching_cues: Plank on forearms with a plate resting on the upper back
Keep a straight line from head to heels
Squeeze glutes and abs the whole time
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike
Using a plate that makes you arch the back
rows.pro_tip: Have a partner place the plate so it does not slide
rows.note: Equipment draft was "other"; mapped to weight plate (proposed token). Check picture for plate vs vest.

rows.name: Machine Front Pulldown
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as the bar rises
coaching_cues: Sit with thighs under the pads, chest tall
Pull the handles to the upper chest, elbows down
Return slowly to a full stretch
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weight
Pulling with the arms instead of the lats
rows.pro_tip: Think elbows to the hips, not hands to the chest
rows.note: Name says Machine; folder is Front Pulldown. Trusted name.

rows.name: Band Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise
coaching_cues: Stand on the band, hold the other end in front
Raise straight arms to shoulder height
Lower slowly against the band tension
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to lift
Raising the arms above shoulder height
rows.pro_tip: Step wider on the band to raise the resistance

rows.name: Barbell Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the bar rises
coaching_cues: Hold the bar shoulder-width in front of the thighs
Raise it to shoulder height with soft elbows
Lower slowly without swinging
common_mistakes: Leaning back to throw the bar up
Raising the bar above eye level
rows.pro_tip: Use an EZ bar or light plates to keep form strict

rows.name: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms rise
coaching_cues: Raise the dumbbells out to the side to shoulder height
Lower, then raise them forward to shoulder height
Alternate the two, keeping the torso still
common_mistakes: Swinging the body to get the weights up
Shrugging the traps
rows.pro_tip: Go lighter than a normal lateral raise
rows.note: Combination of lateral and front raise in one rep.

rows.name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as each arm rises
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench, dumbbells at thighs
Raise one arm to shoulder height, then lower
Alternate arms without leaning back
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso for momentum
Raising the arm above shoulder height
rows.pro_tip: Seated position removes leg drive and keeps it strict

rows.name: Dumbbell Seated Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the arms rise
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench, dumbbells at thighs
Raise both arms to shoulder height together
Lower with control
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weights
Raising the arms above shoulder height
rows.pro_tip: Keep a slight elbow bend to protect the elbows

rows.name: Weighted Front Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise
coaching_cues: Hold a plate at the sides with both hands
Raise it in front to shoulder height
Lower slowly with soft elbows
common_mistakes: Swinging the plate with the hips
Lifting above shoulder height
rows.pro_tip: Grip the plate at 10 and 2 for best control
rows.note: Equipment draft was "other"; assumed a weight plate front raise (could be a dumbbell/sandbag). Check picture.

hold.reason: low-confidence draft with no picture read; the drafted identity is unchecked

rows.name: Barbell Bench Front Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Brace before you sit, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Rack the bar on the front delts, elbows high
Sit back to lightly touch the bench
Stand without rocking, chest upright
common_mistakes: Collapsing the chest onto the bench
Dropping the elbows and losing the bar
rows.pro_tip: Bench sets a consistent depth every rep
rows.note: Assumed box/bench-assisted front squat; a squat rack is implied (no token for rack).

rows.name: Barbell Clean Grip Front Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Brace before you descend, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Clean grip, bar resting on the front delts, elbows high
Squat to at least parallel with a tall torso
Drive up leading with the chest
common_mistakes: Dropping the elbows and losing the rack
Knees caving in on the way up
rows.pro_tip: Strap or lighten the grip if the wrists are stiff

rows.name: Kettlebell Front Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, racked at the chest
Sit down between the hips with an upright torso
Drive up through the heels
common_mistakes: Letting the bell pull the chest forward
Heels lifting off the floor
rows.pro_tip: Two kettlebells in the rack make it a serious leg day
rows.note: Could be single or double kettlebell; picture check optional.

rows.name: Smith Machine Clean Grip Front Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Brace before the descent, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Place feet slightly forward of the bar
Rest the bar on the front delts, elbows up
Squat down and drive up keeping the torso tall
common_mistakes: Feet directly under the bar, loading the knees
Dropping the elbows
rows.pro_tip: Smith machine front squat is easier to balance

rows.name: Full Maltese
rows.breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, avoid the breath hold
coaching_cues: Hold a full planche first, then widen the arms outward
Keep the body completely straight and parallel to the floor
Press the hands down and protract hard
common_mistakes: Rushing to it without years of planche base
Overloading the biceps tendons by skipping progressions
rows.pro_tip: Elite skill; most athletes never need it
rows.note: Extremely advanced; normally done on rings or floor. Equipment draft bodyweight; check picture.

rows.name: Full Planche
rows.breathing_cue: Steady shallow breaths, avoid the breath hold
coaching_cues: Lean far forward on locked straight arms
Lift hips and legs into a straight body line
Squeeze glutes and abs, protract the shoulders
common_mistakes: Bending the arms or piking the hips
Skipping tuck and straddle progressions
rows.pro_tip: Build tuck then straddle planche before attempting full

rows.name: Smith Full Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you drive up
coaching_cues: Place the bar on the upper back, feet slightly forward
Sit down and back to at least parallel
Drive through the whole foot to stand
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward
Heels lifting and the torso folding forward
rows.pro_tip: Feet slightly forward of the bar spare the knees

rows.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale hard as you drive the hips up
coaching_cues: Sit with upper back against the floor or bench, bar over the hips
Plant feet flat and drive the hips up
Squeeze the glutes and hold the top for a second
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
rows.pro_tip: Pad the bar with a towel or foam wrap for comfort
rows.note: Floor bridge with barbell; bench not in the draft.

rows.name: Seated Glute Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, sink deeper on each exhale
coaching_cues: Sit tall, cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back
Hold, then switch legs
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Forcing the knee down
rows.pro_tip: Sit on a chair edge if the floor is too stiff

rows.name: Lying Glutes Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, relax into the stretch
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Pull the thigh toward your chest with both hands
Hold, then switch sides
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and tensing the neck
Pulling hard on the knee joint
rows.pro_tip: Keep the lower back flat on the floor

rows.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at the chest
Sit down between your knees, elbows inside them
Drive up through the heels, chest tall
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the floor
Letting the bell pull the torso forward
rows.pro_tip: Pause 1 second at the bottom to build control

rows.name: Barbell Seated Good Morning
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge forward, exhale as you sit up
coaching_cues: Sit on a bench with the bar on the upper back
Hinge forward with a flat back, hips staying back
Sit up by squeezing the glutes and lower back
common_mistakes: Rounding the back
Using too much weight too soon
rows.pro_tip: Use only a light bar: this is a lower-back builder
rows.note: Bench added to equipment because the exercise is seated; draft listed barbell only.

rows.name: Barbell Stiff Leg Good Morning
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Bar on the upper back, legs nearly straight
Push the hips back and lower the torso with a flat spine
Squeeze the glutes to stand tall
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Locking the knees fully
rows.pro_tip: Go only as low as your hamstrings allow with a flat back

rows.name: Smith Bent Knee Good Morning
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Set the bar on the upper back, knees softly bent
Push the hips back, keep a flat spine
Squeeze the glutes to stand up
common_mistakes: Rounding the back
Letting the knees drift forward as you hinge
rows.pro_tip: Bent knees make it glute-biased and easier on the hamstrings

rows.name: EZ Bar Anti Gravity Press
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with an EZ bar
Press the bar forward and up in an arc
Lower slowly, keeping the chest on the pad
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench
Using momentum from the legs
rows.pro_tip: Go light: rear delts fatigue fast on this lift
rows.note: Sources describe a prone/incline shoulder press with an EZ bar; bench added; targets disputed (rear vs front delts). Check picture.

rows.name: Gripper Hands
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you crush
coaching_cues: Hold the gripper in the palm, handles open
Squeeze the handles fully together
Release slowly to the open position
common_mistakes: Using the thumb-wrist-arm to cheat
Letting the handle snap open
rows.pro_tip: Choose a tension where you reach 10 clean closes
rows.note: Equipment draft was "other"; mapped to grip trainer (proposed token).

rows.name: Barbell Hack Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Brace before you descend, exhale on the drive
coaching_cues: Hold the bar behind the legs, chest up
Squat down with heels flat, bar sliding down the legs
Drive up keeping the bar close to the calves
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Heels lifting off the floor
rows.pro_tip: Heels slightly raised shifts the work to the quads
rows.note: Draft listed barbell + machines; barbell hack squat needs only a barbell, so machines was dropped. Check picture.

rows.name: Smith Hack Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up
coaching_cues: Stand with the bar behind the thighs, heels together-ish
Sit down and back while the bar slides
Press up through the heels
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Letting the knees cave in
rows.pro_tip: Place the feet slightly forward to protect the knees
rows.note: Assumed bar-behind-legs Smith hack squat; check picture for front-loaded variant.

rows.name: Half Pullup
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up
coaching_cues: Hang from the bar and pull up about halfway
Keep shoulder blades pulled down
Lower slowly to a dead hang
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
rows.pro_tip: Use as a bridge toward full pull-ups
rows.note: Folder name is "Bicep Pullup"; name says Half Pullup. Trusted name (partial-range pull-up); check picture.

rows.name: Machine Glute Ham Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Hip pad under the pelvis, feet locked in
Lower the torso with a straight spine
Pull up with the hamstrings and glutes
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Using momentum to pull up
rows.pro_tip: Cross arms on chest to make it harder
rows.note: Tagged knee_dominant (Hamstrings) per the rule for leg-curl type work.

rows.name: Dumbbell Alternate Seated Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall with palms facing in
Curl one dumbbell up, then the other
Keep the elbows pinned to the sides
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso
Letting the elbow drift forward
rows.pro_tip: Alternate arms to keep tension longer

rows.name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Stand with palms facing in
Curl the dumbbell diagonally across the body
Keep the upper arm still
common_mistakes: Swinging the body
Letting the elbow flare out
rows.pro_tip: Aim toward the opposite shoulder for more brachialis

rows.name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Lie back on an incline bench, arms hanging
Curl with palms facing in
Keep the upper arms behind the torso
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows swing forward
Using momentum
rows.pro_tip: The long stretch at the bottom builds the biceps

rows.name: Dumbbell Preacher Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Rest the upper arm on the preacher pad
Curl with a neutral grip, thumbs up
Lower fully without slamming at the bottom
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad
Dropping the weight quickly
rows.pro_tip: Do not fully lock out the bottom if elbows feel sore
rows.note: Preacher bench is the key item; token is bench.

rows.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, arms hanging
Curl with a neutral grip
Squeeze at the top without swinging
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
Rushing the lowering
rows.pro_tip: Chest support removes cheating completely

rows.name: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall on a bench, palms facing in
Curl both dumbbells up, elbows pinned
Lower under control to full extension
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift
Letting the elbows drift forward
rows.pro_tip: Seated position stops hip drive and swinging

rows.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Seated Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Sit tall, one dumbbell with palm facing in
Curl up, elbow pinned to the side
Lower under control
common_mistakes: Leaning to the side
Swinging the weight
rows.pro_tip: Use the free hand to check the elbow stays still

rows.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Standing Hammer Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Stand tall, one dumbbell with palm facing in
Curl up, elbow pinned to the side
Lower under control
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso
Letting the elbow drift forward
rows.pro_tip: Brace the abs so the torso stays still

rows.name: Dumbbell Decline Hammer Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells to the lower chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide
Bouncing the weights off the chest
rows.pro_tip: Neutral grip is gentler on the shoulders

rows.name: Dumbbell Decline Single Arm Hammer Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on a decline bench, one dumbbell, palm in
Lower to the side of the lower chest
Press up without twisting the torso
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to lift
Letting the elbow flare
rows.pro_tip: Brace the core to resist rotation

rows.name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells to the upper chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too steep
Bouncing at the bottom
rows.pro_tip: Neutral grip is gentler on the shoulders

rows.name: Dumbbell Incline Single Arm Hammer Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on an incline bench, one dumbbell, palm in
Lower to the side of the upper chest
Press up without twisting the torso
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to lift
Letting the elbow flare
rows.pro_tip: Brace the core to resist rotation

rows.name: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, palms facing each other
Lower the dumbbells beside the chest
Press up and squeeze the chest
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide
Dropping the weights quickly
rows.pro_tip: Neutral grip keeps the shoulders happy
rows.note: Draft equipment has no bench; may be floor-based. Check picture.

rows.name: Dumbbell Lying Hamstring Curl
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl the heels up
coaching_cues: Lie face down, dumbbell clamped between the feet
Curl the weight toward the glutes
Lower slowly without arching the back
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips off the bench
Dropping the dumbbell on the way down
rows.pro_tip: Ask a partner to place the dumbbell between your feet
rows.note: Bench added (prone on a bench); draft listed dumbbells only.

rows.name: Leg Up Hamstring Stretch
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe slowly, relax as you exhale
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, one leg raised straight
Hold behind the thigh or calf and gently pull
Keep the other leg and lower back flat
common_mistakes: Bending the raised knee too much
Lifting the hips off the floor
rows.pro_tip: Loop a towel around the foot if you cannot reach
rows.indian_alternative: Use a dupatta or towel around the foot

rows.name: Hamstring Walkout
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you walk the feet back in
coaching_cues: Lie on your back in a glute bridge, hips high
Walk the heels out slowly keeping the hips lifted
Walk back in under control
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag as the feet move out
Walking out so far that the hamstrings cramp
rows.pro_tip: Use a shorter walk if the hamstrings cramp
rows.note: Tagged knee_dominant (Hamstrings) per the leg-curl rule; no art for this one.

rows.name: Dumbbell Side Lying One Hand Raise
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the arm lifts
coaching_cues: Lie on your side, dumbbell in the top hand
Raise the arm in a slow arc toward the ceiling
Lower slowly without rolling the torso
common_mistakes: Rolling the body to help the lift
Using too heavy a weight
rows.pro_tip: Very light weights: lying on your side changes the leverage
rows.note: Assumed a side-lying lateral/abduction raise (could be external rotation). Check picture.

Squeeze it hard and hold for a second
Release slowly
common_mistakes: Bending the wrist to cheat
Rushing the release

rows.name: Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bell rises
coaching_cues: Hinge back, bell swinging between the legs
Snap the hips and pull the bell to the rack
Let it settle softly, then switch hands
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of the hips
Letting the bell slam into the forearm
rows.pro_tip: Keep the elbow close and wrap the bell around the wrist

rows.name: Kettlebell Double Alternating Hang Clean
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bells rise
coaching_cues: Hinge back, a bell in each hand
Snap the hips and bring one bell to the rack, then alternate
Keep the torso upright and the bells close
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms
Bells slamming into the forearms
rows.pro_tip: Master the single-bell version first

rows.name: Kettlebell Hang Clean
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as the bell rises
coaching_cues: Hinge back, bell swinging between the legs
Snap the hips and pull the bell to the rack
Let it settle softly at the chest
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of the hips
Letting the bell slam into the forearm
rows.pro_tip: Keep the elbow close and wrap the bell around the wrist

rows.name: Kettlebell Bottoms Up Clean From the Hang Position
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the bell rises, brace the core
coaching_cues: Swing the bell back and pull it up with the bottom facing up
Keep the wrist stacked and gripped hard
Control it at the chest in the rack position
common_mistakes: Letting the bell flip and slam the forearm
Using the arm instead of the hips
rows.pro_tip: Great for grip and shoulder stability, use a light bell

rows.name: Hanging Pike
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as the legs rise
coaching_cues: Hang from the bar, legs straight together
Pike the hips and lift the toes toward the bar
Lower slowly without swinging
common_mistakes: Swinging for momentum
Bending the knees too much
rows.pro_tip: Do hanging knee raises first if you cannot keep the legs straight

rows.name: Alternate Heel Touchers
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe out as you reach each side
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat
Lift the shoulders slightly and reach to touch one heel
Alternate sides without dropping the head
common_mistakes: Pulling on the neck
Moving the hips instead of crunching sideways
rows.pro_tip: Keep the shoulders lifted between reps for constant tension

rows.name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull up
coaching_cues: Wide stance, hold the bell with both hands between the feet
Drive up through the legs and hips
Pull the bell to chin height, elbows high and wide
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms before the hips
Rounding the back at the bottom
rows.pro_tip: Hips drive, arms guide

rows.name: Cable Seated High Row
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull to the face
coaching_cues: Sit tall, cable set above chest height
Pull the handle toward the upper chest or face, elbows high
Squeeze the shoulder blades, return slowly
common_mistakes: Leaning back to swing the weight
Shrugging toward the ears
rows.pro_tip: Elbows high hits the rear delts and upper back
rows.note: High-cable row variant; check picture for grip type.

rows.name: Cable Single Arm Kneeling High Row
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull
coaching_cues: Kneel facing a high cable, one hand on the handle
Pull the elbow back and down toward the hip
Squeeze the shoulder blade, return slowly
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to pull
Shrugging the shoulder
rows.pro_tip: Keep the ribs down so the pull comes from the back
rows.note: Kneeling single-arm high cable row; check picture for pull direction.

rows.name: Machine Single Arm Lateral High Row
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Chest tall on the pad
Drive the elbows down and back
Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Let the lats stretch fully before each rep
common_mistakes: Pulling with the biceps and shrugging the shoulders
Leaning back and swinging the weight
rows.pro_tip: Pause one second with the shoulder blades down.
rows.indian_alternative: Lat pulldown with a resistance band
rows.note: Assumed unilateral plate-loaded high row; check picture for grip and pull angle.

rows.name: Barbell High Bar Squat
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale and brace at the top, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Bar set on the upper traps, chest up, brace the core
Sit down between the hips until thighs are parallel or below
Drive up through mid-foot, knees tracking over toes
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward on the way up
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
rows.pro_tip: Use safety bars or a spotter when going heavy.
rows.indian_alternative: Goblet squat with a heavy backpack
rows.note: Variant of the barbell back squat (bar high on traps); the generic barbell squat should be the core member.

rows.name: Hindu Pushup
rows.breathing_cue: Inhale as you dive forward, exhale as you push back
coaching_cues: Start in a pike with hips high and hands shoulder-width
Dive the chest low between the hands, then sweep up into a cobra
Reverse the path smoothly back to the pike
common_mistakes: Bending the knees and losing the pike
Cranking the lower back in the cobra position
rows.pro_tip: Keep the cobra gentle; lift through the chest, not the lumbar spine.
rows.indian_alternative: Classic Hindu push-up (dand), a traditional akhada move
rows.note: Folder name is Pike to Cobra Pushup; same movement as the Hindu (dand) push-up.

rows.name: Resistance Band Seated Hip Abduction
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you open the knees
coaching_cues: Sit tall with the band just above the knees
Push the knees apart against the band
Return slowly, keeping tension on the band
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso to push the legs out
Letting the band snap back
rows.pro_tip: Lean slightly forward to bias the glutes.
rows.indian_alternative: Resistance band loop from any gym store

rows.name: Side Bridge Hip Abduction
rows.breathing_cue: Breathe steadily; exhale on each leg lift
coaching_cues: Stack feet or stagger them with the hips lifted
Brace the core and keep the body in one line
Move the leg slowly without dropping the hips
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor
Rotating the chest toward the floor
rows.pro_tip: Drop to the knee if you cannot hold a straight line.
rows.indian_alternative: Side plank on a mat
rows.note: Side plank with top-leg raise assumed; confirm which leg lifts.

rows.name: Side Hip Abduction
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift the top leg
coaching_cues: Lie on your side, hips stacked, bottom leg bent
Lift the top leg straight up, toes forward
Lower slowly without resting at the bottom
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward to lift higher
Swinging the leg with momentum
rows.pro_tip: Keep the toes pointing forward, not up, to hit the glute medius.
rows.indian_alternative: Same move on a mat at home
rows.note: Side-lying leg raise assumed; confirm lying vs standing.

rows.name: Cable Hip Adduction
rows.breathing_cue: Exhale as you bring the leg across
coaching_cues: Keep the hips square and stand tall
Sweep the working leg across in front of the standing leg
Return under control without leaning
common_mistakes: Leaning the torso to swing the leg
Using a heavy load and a short range
rows.pro_tip: Slow the return for better inner-thigh tension.
rows.indian_alternative: Side-lying leg raise on the bottom leg
rows.note: Ankle-strap cable adduction.

rows.name: Side Lying Hip Adduction

coaching_cues: Lie on your side with the top leg bent in front
Lift the straight bottom leg toward the ceiling
Lower slowly without touching the floor
common_mistakes: Rolling the hips backward
Swinging the leg with momentum
rows.pro_tip: Slow the return for better inner-thigh tension.
rows.indian_alternative: Side-lying leg raise on the bottom leg
